   wildflowers during brief summers. Snow leopards, mountain goats, and condors navigate cliffs that seem impossible.
   Rivers born from melting glaciers feed millions of people downstream. When we protect mountain ecosystems, we
   protect water, biodiversity, and the cultural traditions of highland communities.

   There is also a stillness in mountains that modern life rarely offers. Above the tree line, with only wind and stone
   for company, the mind slows. Distractions fall away. Many travelers seek mountains not to conquer them, but to be
   changed by them.

   In the end, mountains teach us perspective. They remind us that the highest views require the longest climbs, that
   beauty and hardship often share the same path, and that some of the finest things in life rise quietly above the
   ordinary.
